articles.title: For humanity: China's AI philosophy wins broad international backing
articles.titleCn: 为了人类：中国的人工智能理念赢得广泛国际支持
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping's advocacy for a people-centered approach to artificial intelligence – emphasizing that artificial intelligence should be a trusted, human-controlled tool for the positive, for good and for all – has won broad international support and acclaim.

WAICO "will be able to ensure that we train the necessary talent, we provide the necessary {{6}}.

"We must carry out extensive international cooperation and help Global South countries with {{9}} building to bridge the AI and digital {{10}}, promote {{11}} development, and prevent creating new historical {{12}} in AI," Xi said on Friday. articles.fullText:
Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a keynote speech during the opening ceremony of the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance in Shanghai, east China, July 17, 2026. /Xinhua
Chinese President Xi Jinping's advocacy for a people-centered approach to artificial intelligence (AI) – emphasizing that AI should be a trusted, human-controlled tool for the positive, for good and for all – has won broad international support and acclaim.
In his keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance, Xi put forward a fundamental and vital concept that establishes a philosophical anchor for AI development and governance, according to Katleho Moloi, a professor at the University of South Africa.
"Ultimately, we don't want a system that will replace humanity, but we want a system that will improve the quality of life of humanity," Moloi said of the AI technology in an interview with China Media Group (CMG).
In a nod to the Chinese president's stress that AI's development is to be a trustworthy tool for humanity, he said, "The theme that we believe in is how we can make people's life better, not only by producing techniques that will replace them, but produce techniques that will make whatever they do to be more profitable, and more efficient."
Xi on Friday announced the creation of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO), a Shanghai-headquartered body that aims to ensure that AI is beneficial, safe, fair and serves the benefit of all humanity.
"I fully support President Xi's initiative, and this will augur well for the world," said Liow Tiong Lai, chairman of the ASEAN-China Association for the Promotion of Industrial Cooperation and Development and a former Malaysian transport minister, since the world needs "a body that will be able to promote accessibility and equality."
WAICO "will be able to ensure that we train the necessary talent, we provide the necessary infrastructure. We also share our values so that whatever regulations and whatever AI initiative, it is more humane and it is for the humanity," Liow said.
Public goods that answer the needs of the Global South
Analysts have welcomed Xi's pledge that China, as a responsible major country, is always committed to providing international public goods relating to AI.
"We must carry out extensive international cooperation and help Global South countries with capacity building to bridge the AI and digital divides, promote sustainable development, and prevent creating new historical injustice in AI," Xi said on Friday.
President Xi's emphasis on China as a provider of AI public goods is significant, said Haris Bilal Malik, a researcher at the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad, a think tank in Pakistan.
"It carries a broader meaning that the artificial intelligence is no more an issue of rich countries, or developed countries, or the great powers. It should serve the humanity across the board, across the globe, for every country, especially for the Global South," Malik said.
Donald Ramotar, former president of Guyana, also commended China's key proposals on AI and its push for a governance framework that leaves no nation behind.
China is advocating that the United Nations play a central role in forming "a global AI governance system with broad consensus to benefit all humanity," Ramotar wrote in a recent opinion piece. "This is to ensure that no country is left behind."
A humanoid robot makes balloon animals at the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance in Shanghai, east China, July 18, 2026. 
An open approach that builds global capacity, not walls
The international community has also applauded and embraced China's public pledge to roll out a range of practical measures for global AI capacity building over the next five years.
Xi announced at Friday's gathering that China will provide developing countries with 5,000 opportunities in AI training and seminar programs, and enable 30 countries to use the AI-powered meteorological warning system MAZU, to safeguard homes around the world.
China will also develop international AI application cooperation centers with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, the League of Arab States, the African Union, the Community of Latin American and Caribbean States, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, and BRICS.
Blade Nzimande, Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation of South Africa, hailed the significance of the Chinese concept of building a community with a shared future for humanity and advocating universal participation by all nations in AI development and governance.
African nations lack AI infrastructure, and China has proactively created favorable conditions to enable developing countries to genuinely share in the dividends of AI development, Nzimande said.
Nikki Gastinel, head of the California Software Association, hailed China's approach to AI development as one rooted in openness and the goal of benefiting all.
In expressing her appreciation, Gastinel called on all other nations to build more bridges for communication and cooperation rather than erecting walls that breed division and confrontation.
Xue Lan, dean of the Institute for AI International Governance at Tsinghua University, dismissed the narrative promoted by some in Europe and the United States that frames China and the US as rivals locked in head-to-head AI competition.
Xue said the Chinese president has made it crystal-clear in his speech that China develops AI for the positive, for good and for all humanity, thus spelling out the core purpose of China's AI strategy.

习近平主席于周五宣布成立世界人工智能合作组织，该组织总部设在上海，旨在确保人工智能有益、安全、公平，并服务于全人类的利益。东盟中国工商总会会长、马来西亚前交通部长廖中莱表示：“我完全支持习近平主席的倡议，这对世界来说是个好兆头。”他认为世界需要“一个能够促进可及性和平等性的组织”。

廖中莱说，世界人工智能合作组织“将能够确保我们培养必要的人才，提供必要的基础设施。我们还分享我们的价值观，以便无论何种法规和人工智能倡议，都更加人性化，并服务于人类。”

分析人士对习近平主席的承诺表示欢迎，即中国作为一个负责任的大国，始终致力于提供与人工智能相关的国际公共产品。习近平主席周五表示：“我们必须开展广泛的国际合作，帮助全球南方国家进行能力建设，弥合人工智能和数字鸿沟，促进可持续发展，并防止在人工智能领域制造新的历史不公。”巴基斯坦战略研究所研究员哈里斯·比拉尔·马利克表示，习近平主席强调中国作为人工智能公共产品提供者的角色意义重大。他说：“这具有更广泛的意义，即人工智能不再是富裕国家、发达国家或大国的专属问题。它应该服务于全球所有国家，尤其是全球南方国家。”

圭亚那前总统唐纳德·拉莫塔尔也赞扬了中国在人工智能方面的关键提议，以及推动建立一个不让任何国家掉队的治理框架。拉莫塔尔在最近的一篇评论文章中写道，中国主张联合国在形成“一个惠及全人类的、广泛共识的全球人工智能治理体系”中发挥核心作用。“这是为了确保没有一个国家被落下。”

国际社会还赞赏并欢迎中国公开承诺在未来五年内推出一系列全球人工智能能力建设的实际措施。习近平主席在周五的会议上宣布，中国将为发展中国家提供5000个人工智能培训和研讨项目名额，并使30个国家能够使用人工智能驱动的气象预警系统“妈祖”，以保护世界各地的家园。中国还将与东盟、阿拉伯国家联盟、非洲联盟、拉丁美洲和加勒比国家共同体、上海合作组织以及金砖国家合作开发国际人工智能应用合作中心。

南非科学、技术与创新部长布莱德·恩齐曼迪高度赞扬了构建人类命运共同体的中国理念，以及倡导各国普遍参与人工智能发展和治理的意义。恩齐曼迪表示，非洲国家缺乏人工智能基础设施，而中国积极创造有利条件，使发展中国家能够真正分享人工智能发展的红利。加利福尼亚软件协会负责人尼基·加斯蒂内尔称赞中国的人工智能发展方法植根于开放和惠及所有人的目标。在表达赞赏的同时，加斯蒂内尔呼吁所有其他国家搭建更多沟通与合作的桥梁，而不是筑起滋生分裂和对峙的高墙。清华大学人工智能国际治理研究院院长薛澜驳斥了欧美一些人宣扬的将中国和美国视为人工智能领域针锋相对竞争对手的论调。薛澜表示，习近平主席在讲话中已明确表示，中国发展人工智能是为了积极、有益和全人类的利益，从而阐明了中国人工智能战略的核心宗旨。

articles.title: Nairobi to surpass Cairo and Lagos in metro population by 2050
articles.titleCn: 到2050年，内罗毕将超越开罗和拉各斯成为非洲最大都市区
articles.summary: Kenya's capital is projected to overtake Cairo and Lagos to become Africa's most populous metropolitan area by 2050, highlighting the rapid pace of urbanization reshaping the continent.
articles.summaryCn: 根据经合组织预测，肯尼亚首都内罗毕的都市区人口到2050年将达5720万，超过开罗和拉各斯，成为非洲最大都市区，这反映了非洲快速的城市化进程。

paragraphs.en: Kenya's capital, Nairobi, could {{0}} Cairo and Lagos to become Africa's largest {{4}} region by 2050, according to {{1}} from the Africapolis platform developed by the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), highlighting the rapid pace of {{2}} reshaping the continent. Using Africapolis' methodology, which measures {{3}} built-up metropolitan areas rather than administrative city boundaries, the Nairobi metropolitan region is projected to reach 57.2 million people by 2050, up from an estimated 15.95 million today. Cairo is projected to have 55.5 million {{5}}, while Lagos is expected to reach 36.9 million. The projections reflect Africa's broader {{6}} {{7}}, with the continent expected to account for a significant share of global population growth over the coming decades. As cities expand, they are becoming {{8}} of economic activity, {{9}} and {{23}} development while also facing {{10}} pressure on housing, transport, healthcare and other public services.
paragraphs.cn: 肯尼亚首都内罗毕可能超越开罗和拉各斯，到2050年成为非洲最大的都市区。这一预测来自经合组织开发的Africapolis平台，凸显了重塑非洲大陆的快速城市化进程。根据Africapolis的方法——该方法衡量的是连续建成的大都市区域，而非行政城市边界——内罗毕都市区的人口预计将从目前的约1595万增加到2050年的5720万。开罗预计将有5550万居民，而拉各斯预计将达到3690万。这些预测反映了非洲更广泛的人口转型，预计未来几十年非洲将占全球人口增长的很大一部分。随着城市扩张，它们正成为经济活动、创新和基础设施发展的引擎，同时也面临着住房、交通、医疗和其他公共服务方面的日益增长的压力。

paragraphs.en:
A {{11}} for people and investment
Nairobi's rapid growth has been driven by natural population increase, rural-to-urban {{12}} and expanding economic opportunities that continue to attract people from across Kenya and the wider East African region. An aerial view shows the cityscape and architectural style of Nairobi, the capital of Kenya, November 25, 2018. The city also hosts a sizeable refugee population, alongside a large {{13}} community working in business, {{14}}, technology and international organizations. As Kenya's commercial and financial capital, Nairobi contributes a significant share of the country's GDP. It is home to major banks, multinational companies, technology firms, manufacturers and a {{15}} startup {{16}} that has earned it the nickname "Silicon Savannah."
The continued growth of surrounding areas, including Kiambu, Machakos and Kajiado counties, has transformed Nairobi into a {{17}} metropolitan region, with hundreds of thousands of {{18}} travelling into the city each day.
paragraphs.cn:
吸引人口和投资的磁石
内罗毕的快速增长是由自然人口增长、农村向城市迁移以及不断扩大的经济机会推动的，这些机会持续吸引着来自肯尼亚和更广泛的东非地区的人们。一张航拍图展示了2018年11月25日肯尼亚首都内罗毕的城市景观和建筑风格。该市还拥有大量难民人口，以及庞大的外籍人士社区，他们从事商业、外交、技术和国际组织工作。作为肯尼亚的商业和金融中心，内罗毕贡献了该国GDP的很大一部分。这里拥有主要银行、跨国公司、科技公司、制造商以及一个充满活力的初创企业生态系统，为其赢得了“硅谷稀树草原”的绰号。周边地区（包括基安布、马查科斯和卡贾多县）的持续增长，已将内罗毕转变为一个庞大的都市区，每天有数十万通勤者进入该市。

paragraphs.en:
Planning for a city of the future
County authorities are introducing new planning policies aimed at ensuring Nairobi's expansion remains {{19}} and well managed. Governor Johnson Sakaja says the city's rapidly growing real estate sector requires a stable {{20}} {{21}} to unlock investment while supporting orderly urban development. The Nairobi City County Development Control Policy seeks to {{22}} unplanned construction and provide clear guidance for future land use and physical development. The framework is based on the Nairobi Integrated Urban Development Master Plan (NIUPLAN) and aligns new developments with existing and planned infrastructure capacity. County officials are also expanding {{24}} housing projects to help meet rising demand as the population grows.
paragraphs.cn:
规划未来之城
县级当局正在引入新的规划政策，旨在确保内罗毕的扩张保持可持续和良好管理。州长约翰逊·萨卡贾表示，该市快速增长的房地产行业需要一个稳定的监管框架来释放投资，同时支持有序的城市发展。内罗毕市县级发展控制政策旨在遏制无计划建设，并为未来的土地使用和实体发展提供明确指导。该框架基于内罗毕综合城市发展总体规划，并将新开发项目与现有和规划中的基础设施能力相协调。县级官员还在扩大经济适用房项目，以帮助满足随着人口增长而日益增长的需求。

paragraphs.en:
Urban planners say the reforms are timely, as Nairobi continues to {{25}} with unauthorized developments, building safety concerns and mounting pressure on infrastructure. Without sustained investment, the city could face worsening traffic {{26}}, overcrowded schools and hospitals, rising demand for water and electricity, inadequate sanitation and growing volumes of solid waste. Experts also warn that climate change could intensify these challenges through more frequent extreme weather, flooding and pressure on drainage systems. An aerial view of the city skyline in Nairobi, Kenya, showcases the city's modern architecture, roads, and suburban natural landscape, May 17, 2026. Africa's urban future
The Africapolis projections underscore the rapid evolution of Africa's urban landscape, with metropolitan regions increasingly serving as interconnected economic hubs.

Kenya's capital, Nairobi, could overtake Cairo and Lagos to become Africa's largest metropolitan region by 2050, according to projections from the Africapolis platform developed by the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), highlighting the rapid pace of urbanization reshaping the continent.
Using Africapolis' methodology, which measures contiguous built-up metropolitan areas rather than administrative city boundaries, the Nairobi metropolitan region is projected to reach 57.2 million people by 2050, up from an estimated 15.95 million today. Cairo is projected to have 55.5 million residents, while Lagos is expected to reach 36.9 million.
The projections reflect Africa's broader demographic transformation, with the continent expected to account for a significant share of global population growth over the coming decades. As cities expand, they are becoming engines of economic activity, innovation and infrastructure development while also facing mounting pressure on housing, transport, healthcare and other public services.
A magnet for people and investment
Nairobi's rapid growth has been driven by natural population increase, rural-to-urban migration and expanding economic opportunities that continue to attract people from across Kenya and the wider East African region.
An aerial view shows the cityscape and architectural style of Nairobi, the capital of Kenya, November 25, 2018. 
The city also hosts a sizeable refugee population, alongside a large expatriate community working in business, diplomacy, technology and international organizations.
As Kenya's commercial and financial capital, Nairobi contributes a significant share of the country's GDP. It is home to major banks, multinational companies, technology firms, manufacturers and a vibrant startup ecosystem that has earned it the nickname "Silicon Savannah."
The continued growth of surrounding areas, including Kiambu, Machakos and Kajiado counties, has transformed Nairobi into a sprawling metropolitan region, with hundreds of thousands of commuters travelling into the city each day.
Planning for a city of the future
County authorities are introducing new planning policies aimed at ensuring Nairobi's expansion remains sustainable and well managed.
Governor Johnson Sakaja says the city's rapidly growing real estate sector requires a stable regulatory framework to unlock investment while supporting orderly urban development.
The Nairobi City County Development Control Policy seeks to curb unplanned construction and provide clear guidance for future land use and physical development. The framework is based on the Nairobi Integrated Urban Development Master Plan (NIUPLAN) and aligns new developments with existing and planned infrastructure capacity.
County officials are also expanding affordable housing projects to help meet rising demand as the population grows.
Urban planners say the reforms are timely, as Nairobi continues to grapple with unauthorized developments, building safety concerns and mounting pressure on infrastructure.
Without sustained investment, the city could face worsening traffic congestion, overcrowded schools and hospitals, rising demand for water and electricity, inadequate sanitation and growing volumes of solid waste.
Experts also warn that climate change could intensify these challenges through more frequent extreme weather, flooding and pressure on drainage systems.
An aerial view of the city skyline in Nairobi, Kenya, showcases the city's modern architecture, roads, and suburban natural landscape, May 17, 2026. 
Africa's urban future
The Africapolis projections underscore the rapid evolution of Africa's urban landscape, with metropolitan regions increasingly serving as interconnected economic hubs.
If these projections materialize, Nairobi's rise would reflect not only Kenya's growing economic influence but also East Africa's expanding role in trade, technology and innovation. Urban planners, however, stress that long-term success will depend on sustained investment in housing, transport, public services and climate resilience.

articles.fullText:
As people age, many experience memory decline and slower cognitive processing, along with a higher risk of cerebrovascular disease and cognitive impairment. One important question in aging research is how changes in the brain's blood vessels contribute to cognitive decline.
Scientists from the Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology (SIAT) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have identified a mechanism by which aging weakens the blood-brain barrier, the brain's protective interface with the bloodstream.
The study was published in Neuron under the title "TGF-β1-induced endothelial transcytosis drives blood-brain barrier leakage during aging."
The study shows how aging disrupts transport in brain blood vessel cells, leading to blood-brain barrier leakage. /SIAT
The blood-brain barrier, or BBB, acts as a selective security system. It allows essential nutrients to reach the brain while preventing potentially harmful substances in the blood from entering brain tissue. Damage to this barrier has been linked to cognitive aging, cerebral small vessel disease and several neurodegenerative disorders.
Scientists have traditionally attributed BBB leakage mainly to damage to the tight seals between cells lining brain blood vessels. However, the new study found that another process occurs earlier during aging.
By examining mice at different ages, the researchers found that BBB leakage was already detectable in middle-aged mice and worsened in older animals. The change appeared early in the hippocampus, a brain region important for learning and memory.
At this stage, the seals between blood vessel cells remained largely intact. Instead, the cells' internal transport system became abnormally active, allowing blood-borne substances to pass through the cells and enter brain tissue.
"Rather than first leaking through gaps between cells, the aging blood-brain barrier appears to lose control over transport pathways inside the cells," the researchers said.
The team identified a protein called Mfsd2a as an important part of this protective system. Mfsd2a normally limits unnecessary transport across brain blood vessels. Its levels declined with age, while Caveolin-1, a protein involved in the formation of transport vesicles, increased.
When the researchers restored endothelial Mfsd2a expression or knocked down Caveolin-1 in aged mice, abnormal vesicle transport and BBB leakage were significantly reduced.
The researchers then investigated why Mfsd2a declines during aging. They found that levels of TGF-β1, a signaling molecule involved in inflammation, tissue repair and aging, increased in both the brain and the bloodstream as mice aged.
Excessive TGF-β1 reduced Mfsd2a expression in the cells lining brain blood vessels, causing their transport activity to increase. Raising TGF-β1 levels in young mice caused them to develop several features normally seen in the aged BBB, including increased leakage.
By contrast, blocking TGF-β signaling in aged mice reduced BBB leakage and improved their performance in memory-related behavioral tests.
The findings suggest that age-related BBB damage is not simply the result of passive wear and tear. Instead, it involves biological signals that alter how brain blood vessel cells transport substances.
The study may help explain how vascular changes contribute to cognitive aging. It also points to potential approaches for protecting the aging brain, including maintaining Mfsd2a function or preventing excessive activation of TGF-β signaling. Further research will be needed to determine whether these strategies can be safely translated into treatments for humans.

The WHO expressed particular concern that more than 80% of newly identified infections are not linked to known contacts, indicating undetected chains of transmission. About two-thirds of fatalities occur in communities before patients can access medical care.

As of mid-July, 725 patients were hospitalized or in isolation, and 390 people had recovered. Several treatment centers, however, remain overcrowded.
Research into new medical countermeasures is also advancing. Clinical trials are evaluating monoclonal antibody MBP134 and the antiviral remdesivir, while vaccine studies and post-exposure antiviral research have recently begun.
Ghebreyesus urged the international community to increase financial support, warning that the joint WHO-Africa CDC preparedness and response plan still faces a funding gap exceeding $400 million.
